title: Understanding Gradient Descent
text: Gradient descent is an optimization algorithm used to minimize a function by iteratively moving towards the steepest descent direction. In this problem, we are using it to find the optimal parameters for our model.

title: Analyzing the Loss Function
text: The loss function is defined as the residuals of the model: $$L(theta)=y_i-\operatorname{f_{\theta}}\left(x_i\right)$$. This means we are trying to minimize the difference between the observed value $$y_i$$ and the predicted value $$\operatorname{f_{\theta}}\left(x_i\right)$$.

title: Effect of Gradient Descent on Parameters
text: As we run more iterations of gradient descent, the parameters $$\theta_0$$ and $$\theta_1$$ are updated to minimize the loss function. Consider how the updates affect $$\theta_0$$ over time.

title: Predicting the Behavior of $$\theta_0$$
text: Given the nature of the loss function and the updates in gradient descent, what do you expect will happen to $$\theta_0$$ as the number of iterations increases?
choices: $$\theta_0$$ converges to a finite positive value
